name: Von Flue Choke
keyCorrections: If you can't feel the choke, your shoulder is not deep enough in their neck — adjust your shoulder position.
If they bridge you off, your base is too narrow — widen your knees and lower your hips.
If they roll you during the Von Flue, they have escaped — return to side control or guard.
description: When caught in a guillotine from top position, use shoulder pressure on the opponent's neck combined with chest-to-chest control to reverse the choke and submit them from top position.
shortInstruction: They have a guillotine? Drive your shoulder into their neck, chest-to-chest, and let your body weight do the work.
summary: The Von Flue choke (named after Jason Von Flue) is a counter-submission to the guillotine choke from top position. When your opponent catches you in a guillotine and you cannot escape, you can reverse the submission by driving your shoulder into their neck while maintaining chest-to-chest pressure. The mechanism is a shoulder pressure choke — your shoulder compresses one side of their neck while the figure-four of their own guillotine arm compresses the other side. Their own guillotine grip becomes part of your choke.
whyItWorks: Uses the opponent's own guillotine grip to complete the choke — their arm closes one side, your shoulder closes the other.
Gravity and body weight replace arm strength — you do not need to squeeze, just stay heavy.
It is a perfect counter to the guillotine from top positions (side control, mount, half guard top).
Danaher principle: the Von Flue is the ultimate example of 'use the opponent's attack against them.'
commonMistakes: Panicking and trying to rip your head out — this opens your neck to more pressure.
Not squaring your chest against theirs — chest-to-chest pressure is essential.
Letting them get on top by rolling — maintain top position throughout.
Applying too much shoulder pressure suddenly — apply gradually as their guillotine hand fatigues.
coachingCues: Shoulder in their neck, chest on their chest, stay heavy.
Their grip becomes your choke — let it work for you.
Don't fight the guillotine — use it against them.
Breathe, stay calm, apply slow pressure.
safetySummary: The Von Flue choke compresses the neck — apply gradually and release on tap.
Do not drive your shoulder into their neck explosively.
If you feel your own neck in danger, tap out — the Von Flue is not always the answer.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Guillotine caught from top → don't panic → square chest to their chest → drive your shoulder into their neck → maintain top pressure → wait for the choke.

decisionTree.condition: The Von Flue works best against arm-in guillotines
decisionTree.action: the arm-in creates the closing mechanism.
If the Von Flue fails, switch to breaking their guillotine grip conventionally.

moneyDetails: Position your shoulder directly into the same side of their neck as their choking arm — this creates the closing pressure.
Square your chest against their chest so they cannot bridge or roll you.
Do not try to pull your head out — pushing INTO the guillotine actually relieves neck pressure.
The choke comes from gravity: just stay heavy and breathe — their arm will fatigue and the choke will deepen.
nextStep: After the Von Flue choke, learn to escape the guillotine from top position and the guillotine system.
fixItFast: Not working? Your shoulder may be too low — drive it higher into their neck.
They bridge? Widen your base and stay heavy.
Your neck hurts? Tap and reset — the Von Flue is a counter, not a guaranteed escape.
